reviewNotes.assessment: The memoized object changes on each rendered epoch/connected/pairingId/environment transition. Returning to a previous string value after an intervening transition does not restore the previous owner object. Expiry clears pairingId before the UI permits a new pairing. The outer epoch/connectionId key also remounts the subtree when the connection owner changes. The repeated-ID and environment A-B-A regression cases exercise this distinction.

Cleanup clears only a request whose owner matches that effect, then aborts it. Late callbacks require both the exact request object and current owner object, plus an unaborted controller. Clearing the ref before abort prevents synchronous abort reactions from being treated as current; old cleanup cannot clear a newer owner's request. Unmount has the same ref-clear guard, so it does not rely only on a mounted boolean. The synthetic tests deliberately ignore cancellation and therefore test stale callback rejection independently of real fetch abort.

The visible busy flag is derived from pendingCheck.owner matching the current owner, so stale pending state cannot disable a new pairing. checkRequest is set synchronously before the await and blocks a second click before React renders. Old finally callbacks cannot clear a new request: current() checks both identities and the setPendingCheck updater additionally compares the exact request. The new tests cover duplicate clicks in one batch and stale success/failure while the new query remains pending.

The click handler rejects disconnected, missing, expired and already-claimed pairings. Only the current request may set claimed/error. Current failure releases its busy state; a retry clears its error; claimed=false preserves the code and permits another read; claimed=true hides the code and triggers the pre-existing status refresh. Expiry changes the owner by clearing pairingId. No new timer or automatic pairing creation is introduced.

The owner factory only allocates an object and performs no dispatch. In the normal initial StrictMode effect setup/cleanup replay, no user-triggered status request exists yet. Later owner cleanup clears the matching ref before abort, and a remount creates new refs. No concrete StrictMode defect was established by this static review. The target regressions do not explicitly wrap RemoteSettings in StrictMode, and the inspected test config does not enable a StrictMode wrapper; this path was not separately executed by the cross-reviewer.

The new handler performs only api.call('remoteControl/pairing/status'); it does not use mutate, operation recovery, a retry loop or a polling effect. Pairing creation, enable/disable and client revocation call sites are unchanged. Existing coverage still asserts a single pairing/start across status refresh. The new duplicate-click regression counts status reads rather than adding a write path.

newRegressionReview.coverage: Success/failure after expiry, completing before the new pairing, after it, or during its new status query. Reuses the same pairing ID; asserts new button usability, absent stale error/claimed output, abort signal, exactly two reads and current claimed=true behavior.

Success/failure across disconnect, environment change, environment return A-B-A, connection ID change, epoch change and unmount/remount. Asserts the new request stays busy when the old one finishes, old signal is aborted, old content is absent, and current claimed=false releases the new button.
Current failure and error visibility, retry error clearing, unclaimed success followed by another read, claimed success and exactly three reads.
Two clicks before the pending-state render produce one status read.
